overview: This 640-page file traces U.S. occupation policy on Japanese currency and foreign exchange from 1945 through 1949. Correspondence on blocked yen, remittances, and private claims leads into disputes over the yen-dollar rate, adoption of the 360-yen rate, and Japan’s new foreign exchange and export controls. It includes policy papers, diplomatic correspondence, SCAP directives, legislation, procedures, and forms.
interest: Drafts and interagency correspondence reveal how occupation authorities debated the exchange rate before implementing Japan’s 1949 currency and trade reforms.
